newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end sharply down in all months.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end sharply down in all months.

text.p: All Tokyo corn futures ended sharply lower on Wednesday, with the distant month down by the daily limit of 500 yen, as heavy selling from local investors emerged throughout the day, traders said.
Prices were 270 to 500 yen lower, with the benchmark May 1998 contract down by the limit of 500 yen at 15,180 yen a tonne.
Traders said a weaker Chicago market overnight and the yen's firmer tone against the dollar triggered active selling.
CBOT corn futures ended lower overnight on views that the ongoing speedy pace of corn planting across the U.S. Midwest would result in large yields.
"Some local investors hold many long positions in the Tokyo market. Their long-liquidations were behind heavy price falls today," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot May contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.89-1/2 per bushel at 0650 GMT, against the Tuesday close of $2.88-1/2.
The spot May contract on CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $9.00 at 0650 GMT, up from $8.94 at Tuesday's close.
